speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand your infant is bringing up green, bile-stained vomit and has not passed meconium since birth, along with a swollen belly. To confirm the cause, can you tell me if the baby had a bowel movement within the first 48 hours of life?

speaker: Patient
text: 2-day-old male infant. The infant was born via a home birth without complications. The mother reports that the infant has had bilious vomiting and has not been able to pass meconium since birth. She also notes that the infant's abdomen appears distended.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Hirschsprung Disease.

The failure to pass meconium within 48 hours, combined with bilious vomiting and abdominal distension in a newborn, strongly suggests a distal intestinal obstruction. Given the classic presentation of delayed meconium passage, Hirschsprung disease is the most likely etiology, requiring immediate surgical consultation and further imaging to confirm the diagnosis.
